sense: fitting the person or the occasion

terms.gloss: it is fitting, it becomes, it is proper
terms.grammar: impersonal verb: the thing as subject or an infinitive, the person in the accusative
evidence: Cic. Or. 74: decēre quasi aptum esse cōnsentāneumque temporī et persōnae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Cicero’s own definition: what suits the moment and the person. Dēdecet is the opposite.

evidence: Cic. Sen. 28: est decōrus senī sermō quiētus et remissus
terms.comment: As a noun, decōrum is Cicero’s word for propriety, the Greek πρέπον (Lewis & Short). It can also mean handsome, adorned (poetic).

terms.gloss: it is fitting, it is proper
terms.comment: The impersonal use of conveniō, “come together”, hence “agree, suit”; convenit alone also means “agreed!” (Plaut. Cas. 2.3.54).

phrases.latin: īte procul, juvenēs: mītis mihi convenit aetās: folle decet puerōs lūdere, folle senēs
phrases.english: off you go, young men: a gentle age suits me; the soft ball is right for boys to play with, and for old men
